newsitem.title: USA: Hushed US cash crude markets slide on paper sales.
newsitem.headline: Hushed US cash crude markets slide on paper sales.

text.p: Sharp losses on the NYMEX futures market deflated U.S. cash crude prices Thursday morning ahead of the long U.S. Independence Day weekend.

August West Texas Intermediate/Cushing was 55-60 cents lower in late morning action, around $19.70-80 a barrel. Market movement became more volatile as the morning progressed, leaving August/September rolls at minus 4-8 cents.
Profit-taking keyed outright crude declines, along with the news Iraq and the United Nations finalized an aid distribution plan necessary for restarting stalled "oil-for-food" deal oil sales.
Now that it appears the aid plan is nearly ready for submission for Secretary-General Kofi Annan's approval, the prospect for Iraqi oil liftings becomes closer to reality.
"I think anyone long sour crude in September will be hurt," said a cash trader in Texas.

Most U.N. and senior Iraqi officials expect the oil sales part of the accord to resume in early August, once Annan approves the aid plan and Baghdad issues a new pricing formula required before oil contracts are issued to U.N. overseers.

Domestic grade activity slowed, leaving talked prices at stagnant ranges amid hushed dealings. Many refiners closed operations for the weekend, leaving skeleton crews for handling any last minute trading.

Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James was stuck at 18-19 cents over the August WTI/Cushing marker, steady from Wednesday. Deals were sealed for West Texas Sour/Midland at $1.15 under the benchmark, traders noted.
